note: Reel 30: How Sure Are You? Cut 3's script: after the twist the game runs straight on to its answer, then the real case, then the last question. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart). The officer is am_michael (audition, 10 Nov: no creak on either line). n16 is the same take as n07: the same words, the same voice. Misaki said "drawing" as one syllable (dɹˈYŋ), so n05 has hand-planned phonemes. Facts: docs/research.md.
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You're the only witness. Again.
Watch his face.
This time, he's one of these six, and whoever you pick goes to prison.
Out of ten, how sure are you?
So? Which one?
Good. That's him.
He's a drawing, so he can't see what you picked.
lines.text_kokoro: He's a [drawing](/dɹˈɔːɪŋ/), so he can't see what you picked.

lines.text: So here's the answer.
It's number three.
Look at him.
Now how sure are you that it's him?
It isn't number three.
I made that up.
But he looked right, didn't he?
Was that your memory, or just my voice?
Now watch his eyebrow.
Only one of these six has that cut.
If it isn't the one you picked, an innocent man goes to prison, and he walks.
It's number three.
I lied about lying.
You got a rewind. A real witness doesn't.
In America, one picked a man twice, and police told her so.
In her own words, Bingo. I did it right.
That man was Ronald Cotton. He lost more than ten years.
lines.text_kokoro: That man was Ronald [Cotton](/kˈɑːtən/). He lost more than ten years.

lines.text: Before I said anything, how sure were you?
